Hello, I’m Ila.

I believe in the power of stories. I’m curious about how technology can help us learn from our experiences and tell stories in our own voices.

I’m a Human-Centered Computing Ph.D. student at the University of Florida, where I’m part of the ELX Lab.

I studied computer engineering in Nepal, where teaching children to code sparked my interest in designing technology around people.

EmailLinkedIn ↗

Research

Technology that helps us think, not think for us.

We capture so much of our lives, but how often do we look back? For my dissertation, I want to explore how an AI companion might help college students reflect on everyday experiences while keeping them the authors of their own stories.

I’m also studying whether AI explanations reflect what actually drove its decisions, and how those explanations affect our ability to verify information, the effort it takes, and when we choose to rely on AI.

Teaching & community

It began with learning.

Growing up with parents who were teachers, I learned early that opportunities to learn shouldn’t depend on where we come from.

At Smart Cheli, I taught coding and designed STEAM activities for children in Nepal. I wrote Light Up Kathmandu, a book that teaches coding and electronics through familiar characters and places, and volunteered to translate Scratch into Nepali.

Those experiences still shape how I think about learning and design.

The power of seeing someone like you

I am a founding member of Nepali Women+ in Computing (NWiC). We celebrate the journeys of Nepali women in technology, sharing their challenges, achievements and paths into tech so women and underrepresented communities in Nepal can find role models they relate to.

Our book, Pave the Way, is one part of that effort. Stories can change what we see as possible.

Outside the lab

A few of my favorite things.

Away from my desk, I love growing plants, getting lost in books, making art and trying DIY projects. I sing, listen to music, and occasionally write about technology and culture on Medium.

Let’s connect.

I’m always happy to exchange ideas about research, learning, design, or a good story.
